classification.difficultyReason: In the hardest part, combine equal component segments into equal whole sides and recognise the shared apex angle before forming a SAS proof and deducing corresponding sides.

content.prompt: In each part, first write a congruence statement. Then prove the required result, giving all reasons.

spec.description: Two rotated right triangles, triple ticks MK and PT, double ticks KN and PQ, right angles K and P. Ordinary source blue becomes black.
spec.mathematics: MKN corresponds to TPQ by SAS.

answer.short: $\triangle MKN\equiv\triangle TPQ$ (SAS), so $\angle M=\angle T$ (matching angles).
answer.worked: $MK=TP$ and $KN=PQ$ (marked sides), and $\angle MKN=\angle TPQ=90^\circ$. Hence $\triangle MKN\equiv\triangle TPQ$ (SAS). Therefore $\angle M=\angle T$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).

spec.description: Triangles WDL and MDL share DL; DW and DM have double ticks and the two angles at D are alpha. W, L and M are not collinear. Ordinary source blue becomes black.
spec.mathematics: LDW corresponds to LDM by SAS.

answer.worked: $DW=DM$ (marked sides), $DL=DL$ (common side), and $\angle WDL=\angle LDM=\alpha$. Hence $\triangle LDW\equiv\triangle LDM$ (SAS). Therefore $WL=ML$ (matching sides of congruent triangles).

spec.description: Quadrilateral IJKL with diagonal LJ, right angles I and K and double ticks IL and JK. Ordinary source blue becomes black.
spec.mathematics: JIL corresponds to LKJ by RHS.

answer.worked: $\angle JIL=\angle LKJ=90^\circ$, $JL=LJ$ (common hypotenuse), and $IL=KJ$ (marked sides). Hence $\triangle JIL\equiv\triangle LKJ$ (RHS). Therefore $IJ=KL$ (matching sides of congruent triangles).

spec.description: Straight sides I-H-W and I-G-T with equal double-ticked segments IH, HW, IG and GT. HT and GW intersect at V. Ordinary source blue becomes black.
spec.mathematics: IH=IG; IT=IW by adding equal segments; common included apex angle gives SAS.

answer.worked: $IH=IG$ and $HW=GT$ (marked sides), so $IW=IH+HW=IG+GT=IT$. Also $\angle HIT=\angle GIW$, since $IH$ lies along $IW$ and $IG$ lies along $IT$. Hence $\triangle HIT\equiv\triangle GIW$ (SAS). Therefore $HT=GW$ (matching sides of congruent triangles).
